correctness.rationale: For S_j=x^TH^jx, m=S2/S1 and variance v=S3/S1−m², expanding the update gives (1+σ²v)/(1+σm)². Endpoint inequality v≤(b−m)(m−a) is sharp for any actual extremal eigenspaces. Independent SymPy differentiation produced the affine derivative numerator σ[σ(a+b)+2σ²ab−2−σ(2+σ(a+b))m]; substitution of stationary m verified the quoted second rational branch identically. The branch switch, unique σ minimax point, and κ descent frontier follow from derivative and AM–GM with attainable two-point mass. Independent exact witness at H=diag(1,10), σ=2 is alpha=12/31 and ratio=41/31.
residual_risks: Only centered zero-minimum SPD quadratics in exact arithmetic, deterministic update and one step; no implication for long-run stability or stochastic gradients.

value.rationale: The exact worst one-step objective factor for a named adaptive optimization method is a natural benchmark. Separating universal one-step descent, regularization that minimizes worst-case loss, and transient objective spikes gives a meaningful calibration boundary and explicit extremizers across every SPD dimension.
residual_risks: The result is not a multistep convergence theory or a recommendation for stochastic training.

final_claim: The deterministic NGN step on an SPD quadratic has a sharp two-branch all-state objective factor; its unique minimizing regularization is 2(a+b)/(b−a)², and universal one-step descent for every positive σ holds exactly when κ≤3+2√2, otherwise only σ≤2/(a+b−2√(2ab)) is safe.
